Trying to Conceive

Viagra and other erection medicines: differences and safe use

Updated: October 12, 2026

Written and edited by BeMama Authors team: checked against published guidance from recognized health organizations.

Viagra is a brand of sildenafil, one of several oral medicines for erectile dysfunction (ED). Cialis contains tadalafil, Levitra is a vardenafil brand, and Stendra contains avanafil. They belong to the phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitor group. The right choice depends on health, other medicines, preferred timing and response, rather than a universal best or safest tablet.

What these medicines do

During sexual stimulation, nitric oxide helps increase cyclic GMP, a signal that relaxes smooth muscle in the penis and allows blood to enter. PDE5 inhibitors slow the breakdown of that signal. Sexual stimulation is still needed; a tablet does not automatically produce an erection or increase desire.

They may help achieve and maintain an erection, but do not cure every underlying cause of ED, prevent pregnancy or protect against sexually transmitted infections. Recurrent erection difficulties deserve assessment of physical health, medicines, mental health and sexual concerns, without shame or pressure to perform.

Assessment before choosing treatment

A clinician may ask about erections, ejaculation, orgasm, desire, existing conditions and all prescribed medicines, supplements and recreational drugs. Examination and selected tests can help identify vascular, nerve, hormonal or structural problems. ED can accompany diabetes or cardiovascular disease; buying a tablet should not replace this assessment.

Discuss whether sexual activity and a PDE5 inhibitor are suitable, especially with heart disease, recent heart attack or stroke, blood-pressure problems, kidney or liver disease, previous serious eye or hearing problems, or a tendency to prolonged erections. Do not stop another prescription independently because you suspect it contributes to ED.

Cialis compared with Viagra

Tadalafil can provide an opportunity to respond to stimulation for up to 36 hours after an as-needed dose. This is not a continuous erection, a guarantee of response, or the time until all medicine leaves the body. Sildenafil is generally used before an anticipated occasion and has a shorter treatment window.

Tadalafil also has a prescribed once-daily regimen and is approved for symptoms of benign prostate enlargement, including when ED coexists. Daily and as-needed plans are different: do not add extra tablets for sex or switch between them yourself. Back or muscle pain can occur with tadalafil, but such symptoms are not exclusive to it.

Levitra compared with Viagra

Vardenafil tablets are generally taken about 60 minutes before anticipated sexual activity. Sildenafil is usually taken about an hour beforehand; its US label permits a window from 30 minutes to 4 hours before sex. Individual response varies, so these times are planning guidance, not a countdown guaranteeing an erection.

Neither medicine can be declared free of rash, muscle symptoms or visual effects. Vardenafil has a particular heart-rhythm precaution: people with congenital long-QT syndrome or taking certain rhythm medicines should avoid it. Tell the prescriber about rhythm problems and all medicines before selecting an alternative.

Stendra compared with Viagra

Avanafil may be prescribed for use as early as about 15 minutes before sex at some strengths; the lower strength has a different timing instruction, about 30 minutes. Follow the instructions for the exact prescribed product. A faster possible onset does not establish that it is better for everyone.

Avanafil can cause headache, flushing, nasal symptoms, back pain and sore throat, as well as serious class warnings. It is not a medicine with only one side effect, nor is it guaranteed to avoid vision or hearing problems. Current brand and generic availability depends on the country and product; ask a licensed local pharmacist.

Vardenafil compared with tadalafil

The important distinction is not simply which works first. Tadalafil offers a longer response window and a separate daily option; vardenafil is used as needed. Tadalafil can also treat prostate-enlargement symptoms under a clinician’s plan, whereas that is not the indication of the vardenafil label discussed here.

Both can cause unwanted effects and lower blood pressure. Choice should consider interactions, heart-rhythm risk, kidney and liver function, cost and personal preferences. If one is unsuitable or ineffective, ask for review rather than combining medicines or borrowing another person’s prescription.

Strengths, food and storage

Tablet strengths are not interchangeable doses. Examples in US labels include sildenafil 25, 50 and 100 mg; vardenafil 2.5, 5, 10 and 20 mg; and avanafil 50, 100 and 200 mg. Tadalafil labels describe low-dose daily and higher as-needed regimens; the current branded Cialis listing shows 5, 10 and 20 mg tablets, while regimen and product availability differ. These numbers are identification information, not a recommendation to choose or increase a dose. Medical conditions and interactions may require lower doses or longer intervals, not simply one dose every day.

Food instructions differ. A high-fat meal can delay sildenafil, affect vardenafil absorption and delay avanafil absorption, although the latter two labels allow use with or without food. Tadalafil can be taken without regard to meals. Ask about alcohol, which can impair erections and add dizziness or low blood pressure. Store the exact product as its leaflet directs, generally at controlled room temperature, away from children; avanafil also needs protection from light.

Interactions that can make treatment dangerous

Do not use these medicines with nitrates for angina or recreational nitrite ‘poppers’, or with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat. Dangerous blood-pressure lowering can result. Alpha blockers, other blood-pressure medicines and drugs affecting CYP3A4, including some HIV medicines, antibiotics and antifungals, require a specific interaction check; some combinations must be avoided.

Do not combine ED tablets with each other or with another product containing the same ingredient, including some pulmonary-hypertension treatments. Do not add injections or other erection treatments without a specialist plan. Give every clinician and pharmacist an up-to-date medicine list. Longer action, particularly with tadalafil, means interactions may persist beyond the intended sexual occasion.

Side effects and immediate warning signs

Headache, flushing, indigestion, nasal congestion and dizziness can occur; some products also cause nausea, back or muscle pain, rash or visual changes. Ask about effects that bother you or persist. Do not drive with dizziness or impaired vision. Frequencies from different studies do not prove one medicine is safest for you.

An erection reaching 4 hours needs immediate emergency care, even without pain; seek help sooner for a painful persistent erection. Stop the medicine and obtain immediate medical attention for sudden vision loss or sudden hearing decrease or loss. Chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, fainting or loss of consciousness, or serious allergy signs need emergency help. Stop sexual activity, tell responders the exact drug and last dose, and do not take your own nitrate for chest pain after an ED tablet.

Cost, access and reliable supplies

Price, generic options, prescription or pharmacist access and insurance coverage vary by country, product and plan. Ask a licensed pharmacy for the exact ingredient, strength, legal access requirements and total cost; there is no universal coverage or availability promise. A cheaper tablet is not automatically the same regimen or a suitable substitute.

Avoid unverified online sellers and ‘natural Viagra’ or sexual-enhancement supplements. Some contain undeclared prescription ingredients and can interact dangerously with nitrates or other medicines. A positive review or absence from a warning list does not establish safety. Discuss any supplement before use.

If the first medicine does not help

Review how the prescribed medicine was used, stimulation, food, expectations and side effects with the prescriber. A clinician may adjust treatment or select another option; do not take an extra dose or switch yourself after a disappointing attempt. There is no obligation to have sex, and a partner’s preferences should be discussed with consent.

Managing contributing conditions and supportive changes such as stopping smoking, appropriate physical activity and moderating alcohol may help. Counseling, a vacuum device, clinician-taught medicines delivered locally or a penile implant are options for selected people. ‘Natural’ remedies are not proven substitutes for assessment, and no treatment guarantees a particular sexual result.

Evidence-informed guidance

What trusted health organizations recommend

Arrange assessment for recurrent erection difficulties and bring a complete medicine, supplement and recreational-drug list.

Ask a prescriber or pharmacist to explain your exact product, timing, food instructions and interaction precautions; do not combine, self-switch or increase treatment.

Use emergency care for warning signs, and reliable licensed supplies rather than unverified sexual-enhancement products.

How BeMama can help

BeMama can help organize questions, medicine lists and notes about timing or side effects for a clinical appointment. It cannot diagnose ED, check every interaction, select a dose or decide whether sexual activity or a medicine is safe. Do not wait for an app response with an emergency symptom.

When to seek help

Seek emergency care for an erection reaching 4 hours, or sooner if painful and persistent; sudden loss of sight or sudden hearing decrease or loss needs immediate medical attention. Chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, fainting or loss of consciousness, or serious allergy signs require emergency help. Stop sex, disclose the drug and last dose, and do not self-administer nitrates. Never combine ED medicines or choose a dose from this article.

Evidence notes updated: October 12, 2026

Key takeaways

  • Sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil and avanafil assist the response to stimulation; they do not automatically cause desire or an erection.
  • Timing, food effects and daily versus as-needed regimens differ; a 36-hour response window is not a 36-hour erection.
  • Nitrates, poppers and guanylate cyclase stimulators are dangerous combinations; check every medicine and never combine or self-switch ED treatments.
  • An erection reaching 4 hours, sudden sight or hearing loss, chest pain or loss of consciousness needs immediate medical help.
  • Choose treatment after assessment, using a reliable pharmacy and an individual prescription; no tablet is universally best or free of side effects.

Frequently asked questions

How does Viagra work?

Sildenafil inhibits PDE5 and helps preserve the cyclic-GMP signal generated during sexual stimulation, allowing more blood into the penis. It needs stimulation and does not automatically produce desire or cure the cause of ED.

Is Levitra better than Viagra?

There is no universal winner. Timing, response, interactions and side effects matter. Vardenafil has an additional long-QT and rhythm-medicine precaution; neither drug is free of visual or other unwanted effects.

Is Stendra safer or faster?

Some prescribed avanafil strengths may be used about 15 minutes before sex, but the lower strength has different instructions. Faster possible onset does not prove superior safety, and serious erection, vision, hearing and blood-pressure warnings still apply.

Is Levitra better than Cialis?

Tadalafil has a longer response window, a prescribed daily option and an indication for prostate-enlargement symptoms. Vardenafil is an as-needed ED treatment. A clinician should match either option to health, interactions and preferences.

Does 36 hours mean an erection for that long?

No. It describes a possible period of improved response to stimulation after tadalafil, not a continuous erection or complete drug clearance. An erection reaching 4 hours is an emergency; do not wait for the medicine to wear off.

Can I choose a dose from a comparison table?

No. Strengths and regimens are drug- and product-specific. Kidney or liver disease and interactions may require a lower dose, longer interval or another treatment. Follow your own prescription and ask before changing it.

What should I do about chest pain after a tablet?

Stop sexual activity and seek emergency help. Tell responders which medicine you took and when. Do not take a nitrate yourself because the combination can dangerously lower blood pressure; the emergency team must decide treatment.

What if tablets do not work or I prefer another approach?

Ask for assessment and a review of use rather than combining or repeating doses. Treating contributing conditions, counseling, a vacuum device or specialist treatments may be appropriate. Avoid unverified sexual supplements and do not let performance pressure override consent.

This article is general education, not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always talk with a qualified healthcare professional about your situation, and seek urgent care for emergencies.
